big.message: [SpeedVsTime!B2:B1894] 1 of 50 samples (2.0%) in the speed trace imply accelerations beyond tyre grip. The worst is +30 mph in one 2000 ms sample at index 0, which is +2.5 g — no car does that, so it is a logging or data-entry artefact, not vehicle behaviour. This matters because the m*a term turns every one of those steps into a current spike and then into a thermal load. The workbook never differentiates its speed trace, so it never notices; it also therefore has no acceleration term at all, which is why its currents are low. Fix the trace, or pass smooth_window to filter it and accept that the peaks are approximate.

[ElecPropulsion!B1] Peak required motor torque 121 Nm at a 7:1 reduction exceeds the motor's 120 Nm peak. Gearing up is the fix — torque scales inversely with the reduction, while pack current does not change at all, because power is force times speed regardless of what gear delivers it. That last point is why the workbook's fifteen-column current sweep could never have informed a gear choice.
